slices.focus: Tasha tries beginner birding at Yates Mill; discovers the restoration of quiet focused attention
slices.summary: During a calmer patch at work, Tasha joins a Saturday beginner bird-walk at Yates Mill, invited by Lena Morales (a volunteer coordinator from another nonprofit). Borrowing binoculars, she discovers the experience completely absorbs her attention — she goes solid stretches without mentally scanning for someone else's crisis for the first time in memory. The agent helps her recognize this as 'recovery time' rather than a hobby, plan to protect a couple of early Saturdays each month, keep the gear borrowing to avoid premature commitment, and experiment with solo early-morning loops on non-walk weeks. Tasha treasures being a beginner in public after so much of her life depends on competence, and appreciates having a friend who texts 'want to look at birds this Saturday — yes or no.'
